pose.name: ready
pose.why: Where the full arm waits: it starts and ends every session here and arm-hold holds it here between them (never released). Zach 2026-11-19: 'a better Home/ready position that is lower energy and more centered in the belt'. The upper arm 5 deg forward of vertical, the forearm 55 deg forward, J1 -2, the claw lying flat along the plane: the claw's tip over the belt's usable middle (bench plane x 0.177 m; the arm reaches hover height from x -0.10 to 0.45) at 2.5 W copper to hold (PID tuna's 15c masses; the 2026-11-15 READY took 3.9 W with the hand 478 mm out past the far rail), 120 mm over the belt and 55 mm over the tallest item, the bundle's self-collision rules proven, 0.6 % of the overhead camera's pick zone hidden. WHY the claw flat: on this five-bar a plumb claw needs the wrist ~100 mm higher to clear the items, and every claw-plumb pose that holds with less than the old READY sits at the far rail (x >= 0.44); a session leaves READY with a wrist swing in place and ends with one back (repick). WHY J1 -2, not 0: the bench admits J1 only in [-90, 0] (full_arm_pan.J1_PAN_RANGE_RAD), so a hold that sags a tenth of a degree past 0 would refuse a session. The study: bam_ws reports/media/ready-pose-2026-11-19.html (variant F). The rack realises it per power-up as a board record (ready_record.json, which carries this pose's digest): python -m bam_rack_twin.hardware.zero_writer ready writes it after an edit here.

pose.name: homing
pose.why: The homing routine's posture: READY's numbers from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-19 (the claw's TCP 40 mm over the bin's drop, TCP (0.565, 0.400) m in the bench plane, the claw plumb (TD4: W1 = L2's angle, W2 +90, W3 0); the five-bar as sim2real's homing ruler had it, Craig 65.246 / 122.791; J1 -12.7). WHY homing keeps its own pose when READY moves: J1 seeks its top stop with the arm in this posture, where J1's gravity at the stop measured 5.2 N.m against the seek's 9 N.m stall rule (sim2real j1_home); in READY's compact posture the model's gravity there is 1.6x (study: -6.7 vs -4.1 N.m), which would leave too little between gravity plus friction and the rule to tell the stop from a stall. The wrist feed-forward and the homing corridor were fitted and proven here, byte for byte. After homing the arm is walked to READY (bam_robot_activity.runner --return-home).

pose.name: home
pose.why: The five-bar's home in its homed map of record (homed_083647, 2026-11-10: home_joint_rad, Craig 91.01 / -126.438): where fivebar_home ends and the homing routines start their walks (sim2real gff_rung / fullarm_check / fullarm_home HOME_CRAIG_DEG, bam_rack_twin fullarm_comp's 'home'). The full arm never waits here in a session: the claw would hang 101 mm into the belt.
